q: Calculate the percentage decrease in deer density over 10 years.
Describe the relationship between deer density and willow seedlings.
As deer fell, seedlings rose more than fivefold (2 to 11 per m²): a negative relationship.
Name the type of control shown, and explain it.
Top-down control (a trophic cascade): the predator limits the herbivores, which lets the plants recover.
Time by rivers fell even more than deer numbers. Suggest why this matters.
Deer avoid open riverbanks where wolves hunt, so riverside willows are browsed much less even where deer remain; more willows support more beavers.
Suggest one other explanation for the rise in seedlings, and how you could test it.
For example wetter years or less hunting by people. Compare with similar valleys without wolves over the same years, or use fenced plots that keep deer out.
